A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgenticLU study and contain readable text, figures, tables, and appendices. The added appendix and retained material can be matched reliably across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original long-context and short-context benchmark evaluations, component ablations, reasoning-round comparisons, and inference-overhead measurements in Sections 6–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a prompting-only evaluation of the agentic workflow in Appendix C and Table 9.

M1.justification: The CoC self-clarification and pointback workflow, tree-search trace construction, and SFT followed by DPO remain unchanged. The new prompting-only experiment evaluates a comparison variant without modifying the proposed AgenticLU procedure.

E1.justification: NarrativeQA training, seven long-context evaluation tasks, and six short-context benchmarks are retained. The new experiment reuses HotpotQA, Natural Questions, PopQA, and TriviaQA at the existing 128K context length.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds 'Llama-3.1-8B + Prompting Only,' applying the agentic workflow without AgenticLU finetuning, alongside the base and trained models on four QA tasks. The original benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a control that omits AgenticLU finetuning while applying its workflow at 128K tokens. Existing experiments retain their context lengths, evaluation metrics, judging procedure, and training settings; no revision to those protocols is reported.

E4.justification: v1 studies reasoning rounds, removal of clarification or pointback, and runtime overhead. v2 retains these analyses and adds a focused test of whether the complete workflow is effective without finetuning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The new comparison likewise provides point estimates without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports prompting-only accuracies of 53.3 on HotpotQA, 56.7 on Natural Questions, 51.6 on PopQA, and 72.8 on TriviaQA, averaging 58.6. These entries were absent from v1. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 9–15, renumbered 10–16 in v2.

T1.justification: The methodological definitions and reasoning are retained. Neither version contains a formal theorem or proof development, and v2 adds no mathematical derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about self-taught long-context understanding, CoC path construction and distillation, benchmark performance, and preserved short-context capabilities. The added control supplies supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds the interpretation that clarification can help multi-hop QA without finetuning, but difficulty identifying relevant paragraphs limits the base model's overall benefit. The existing limitation concerning fixed reasoning depth remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The hardware, software frameworks, SFT/DPO hyperparameters, processing details, prompt templates, and code/data access statement are retained. The workflow and evaluation templates move from Appendices D/E to E/F without substantive changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the cited works are unchanged. The new experiment adds no citations or substantive revision to the paper's positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a short Appendix C and a funding acknowledgement, and updates affected cross-references and appendix letters. The existing scientific prose and main section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, rearranges the appendix result tables, and moves the evaluation-template box to the final page. Page-number footers are removed. Figures 1–3 and the existing table content and designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new same-workflow, prompting-only control addresses an omission in v1's evidence about training's contribution. Table 9 reports averages of 58.6 for prompting alone, 58.2 for the base model, and 75.7 for trained AgenticLU, strengthening the empirical case for finetuning. This is a focused improvement on four existing 128K tasks; the proposed paragraph-identification explanation is not directly measured, and uncertainty reporting remains absent.
